subtitle: Eighteen Offices for a Restless Kingdom

panels.shot: low-angle wide inside a dim palace hall, rows of palm-leaf records and clerks fading into shadow behind a solitary ruler
panels.action: Chikka Devaraja Wodeyar stands in regal stillness amid a hall crowded with scribes and palm-leaf bundles, his gaze fixed on a distant map of Mysore as lantern light glows on stacked records.

dialogue.text: In a time of sieges and coins, Chikka Devaraja Wodeyar dared to do what few war-lords tried: he turned a marching kingdom into eighteen watching offices.

i18n.hi: घेरों और सिक्कों के दौर में चिक्का देवराज वोडेयर ने अनोखा कदम उठाया – चलते फ़िरते राज को अठारह चौकस दफ्तरों में बदल दिया।

panels.shot: slow push-in from bird’s-eye over Srirangapatna fortress to a medium shot of the young king in council
panels.action: The island fortress of Srirangapatna rises from the Kaveri, its walls bristling with cannon, as inside a younger Chikka Devaraja Wodeyar leans over a low table strewn with maps and revenue rolls.

dialogue.text: When Chikka Devaraja took the ivory throne of Mysore, the Kaveri island of Srirangapatna was his shield, but beyond its walls, larger powers circled like hawks.

i18n.hi: जब चिक्का देवराज ने मैसूर का हाथीदांत सिंहासन संभाला, कावेरी की श्रीरंगपट्टन द्वीप ढाल थी, पर किले के बाहर बड़े साम्राज्य गिद्धों처럼 मंडरा रहे थे।

panels.shot: wide map-table shot, candlelit, with shadows of imagined enemies looming on the wall
panels.action: By candlelight, Chikka Devaraja traces border lines on a rough map showing Mysore hemmed between the Mughal north, Maratha west, and coastal powers, their silhouettes looming as ghostly shadows on the wall.

dialogue.text: To the north, Aurangzeb’s empire pressed down; to the west, Maratha horsemen rode; on the coasts, new Europeans counted ports and pepper.

i18n.hi: उत्तरी आसमान से औरंगज़ेब का साम्राज्य झुका, पश्चिम से मराठा घुड़सवार टूट पड़े, तटों पर नए फिरंगी बंदरगाह और काली मिर्च गिनते रहे।

panels.shot: dynamic mid-shot of Chikka Devaraja mounted, with marching columns stretching into the horizon
panels.action: Armoured yet simply dressed, Chikka Devaraja rides at the head of Mysore’s troops along a dusty road, banners of the royal boar fluttering as village fields blur past under marching feet.

dialogue.text: He chose not only to endure these storms, but to grow inside them, extending Mysore’s banner over new forts, forests and tank-fed fields.

i18n.hi: उसने इन तूफ़ानों से बस बचना ही नहीं, उन में बढ़ना चुना, मैसूर का ध्वज नए किलों, जंगलों और सरोवरों से सिंचे खेतों पर फैलाया।

panels.shot: wide shot of Bangalore fort from outside, with two parties facing each other, deed held between them
panels.action: Outside the sturdy walls of Bangalore fort, Chikka Devaraja stands with a small retinue, accepting a palm-leaf deed from imperial agents as soldiers watch and the town’s tiled roofs rise behind the ramparts.

dialogue.text: In 1687, he seized a quiet opening: he bought Bangalore from the Mughal authorities, turning a garrison town into his key to the plateau.

i18n.hi: १६८७ में उसने मौक़ा लपका – मुग़ल अामिलों से बैंगलूर खरीदा, चौकीदार कस्बे को पठार की अपनी चाबी बना दिया।

panels.shot: intimate interior shot of a Mughal-style hall in Mysore, with an envoy bowing and Chikka Devaraja seated formally
panels.action: In a hall softened by carpets and carved pillars, a richly robed envoy bearing Northern dress bows before Chikka Devaraja, who listens gravely, a scroll sealed with a Persian script resting on a stand nearby.

dialogue.text: With Aurangzeb’s court he played a careful game, sending and receiving envoys, reading the language of farmans and Persian chancery practice as closely as he studied battlefields.

i18n.hi: औरंगज़ेब के दरबार से वह नपे-तुले खेल खेलता रहा, दूत भेजता–बुलाता, फ़रमानों और फ़ारसी कचेहरी की लिखत उसी लगन से पढ़ता जैसे रणभूमि।

panels.shot: over-the-shoulder shot of Chikka Devaraja studying a Persian-style document while native scribes wait nearby
panels.action: Seen from behind, Chikka Devaraja examines a parchment bearing neat Persian script, while Mysore scribes, their stylus and palm leaves ready, wait for his word to translate and adapt its forms.

dialogue.text: From these contacts, he saw that empire was not only spears and elephants; it was ink, ledgers and officers whose signatures bit as sharply as swords.

i18n.hi: इन मुलाक़ातों से उसने समझा, साम्राज्य सिर्फ़ भाले और हाथी नहीं – स्याही, बहियां और ऐसे अफ़सर जिनके दस्तख़त तलवार जितने तेज़ काटते।

panels.shot: medium shot in an old audience hall, with villagers and officers together, confusion evident
panels.action: In an older, crowded audience hall, petitioners, tax-collectors and soldiers shout over one another before Chikka Devaraja, who sits still but frowning, as loose palm leaves and coins lie scattered on the floor.

dialogue.text: Yet inside Mysore, the machinery creaked; decisions jammed in the king’s hall, revenues leaked, and no one knew precisely whose hand held which duty.

i18n.hi: पर मैसूर की भीतर की चक्की चरमराती रही – फ़ैसले दरबार में अटकते, महसूल टपकता, और किसी को साफ़ न था कौन किस काम का मालिक है।

panels.shot: close-up on Chikka Devaraja’s face, half lit, half in shadow, as he listens to overlapping voices
panels.action: A close view of Chikka Devaraja’s lined face shows one eye narrowing in thought as the blurred forms of a merchant, a soldier and a village headman lean inward, each pleading their case at once.

dialogue.speaker: chikka_devaraja_wodeyar
dialogue.text: One mouth cannot hear every quarrel. The kingdom will choke on its own words.

i18n.hi: एक ही कान हर झगड़ा नहीं सुन सकता। राज्य अपनी ही बातों में घुट जाएगा।

panels.shot: wide overhead shot of a newly built administrative hall, orderly desks in rows
panels.action: A new, airy hall in Mysore shows rows of low desks, each with clerks seated before neat bundles of records, as Chikka Devaraja walks a central aisle, hand lightly touching a carved pillar.

dialogue.text: His answer was simple and radical: divide the work, fix the duties, and bind the kingdom’s business into eighteen watching offices—the Attara Kacheri.

i18n.hi: उसका नुस्ख़ा सीधा पर कड़क था – काम बाँटो, जवाबदेही तय करो, और राज्य का सारा कारोबार अठारह चौकस कचेरियों में बाँध दो – अत्तारा कचेरी।

panels.shot: series-like composition within one frame, showing three different desks in the hall handling distinct tasks
panels.action: Within the same hall, one desk tallies grain and copper coins, another copies royal orders onto palm leaves, while a third discusses frontier postings with a map, as Chikka Devaraja observes from the background.

dialogue.text: Some offices watched the land and its grain, others the king’s orders, others the men and horse that marched at his word; each had its place in the new order.

i18n.hi: कुछ दफ़्तर ज़मीन और अनाज पर नज़र रखते, कुछ राजा के हुक्म पर, कुछ उसके शब्द पर चलने वाले सिपाहियों और घोड़ों पर; हर एक की जगह नए इंतज़ाम में तय थी।

panels.shot: medium shot of Chikka Devaraja instructing a senior official in the hall
panels.action: Standing beside a senior official holding a stylus, Chikka Devaraja gestures firmly toward the far end of the hall where junior clerks work, his face intent, the official bowing slightly in acknowledgement.

dialogue.speaker: chikka_devaraja_wodeyar
dialogue.text: Let each office answer for its own lapses. No more confusion hidden in crowds.

i18n.hi: हर दफ़्तर अपना हिसाब ख़ुद देगा। अब भीड़ के पीछे छिपी गड़बड़ नहीं चलेगी।

panels.shot: intimate study shot as he writes or dictates to a court poet, with manuscripts piled nearby
panels.action: In a quieter chamber, Chikka Devaraja sits cross-legged beside a court poet, dictating as the poet writes on a palm leaf; nearby rest bound manuscripts labeled in ornate Kannada script.

dialogue.text: He did not only arrange offices; he patronised words, commissioning works like the Gitagopalam and Chikadevaraya Binnopam, polishing his image as a guardian of Kannada and Srivaishnava learning.

i18n.hi: वह सिर्फ़ कचेरी नहीं सजाता था; शब्दों का भी सह patron था, गीता गोपालम और चिक्कदेवराय बिन्नोपम जैसे ग्रंथ लिखवाकर खुद को कन्नड़ और श्रीवैष्णव विद्या का रक्षक चमकाता रहा।

panels.shot: wide shot of Nanjanagudu countryside, with peasants and Jangama leaders confronting royal officers
panels.action: On the open fields near Nanjanagudu, peasants stand beside Jangama religious leaders, faces set and arms folded, as royal tax officials on horseback confront them under a hot, unforgiving sky.

dialogue.text: But if offices need silver, someone must pay. Around Nanjanagudu, Jangama-backed villagers resisted taxes they felt broke old understandings.

i18n.hi: पर दफ़्तर चलें तो चाँदी भी लगे; फिर देगा कौन? नंजनगुड के आस–पास जंगमों की पीठ वाले गाँव वाले उन महसूलों के ख़िलाफ़ खड़े हो गए जिन्हें वे पुरानी बोली तोड़ना मानते थे।

panels.shot: tense mid-shot of a Jangama leader raising his hand, with villagers behind and soldiers ahead
panels.action: A Jangama leader in simple robes stands between villagers and approaching Mysore soldiers, one hand raised in defiance, his gaze steady, as lances glint in the distance.

dialogue.text: They stood not only as taxpayers, but as followers of an old Shaiva path, challenging the king’s demand to push deeper into their fields and shrines.

i18n.hi: वे सिर्फ़ करदाता नहीं, पुरानी शैव परंपरा के अनुयायी बनकर खड़े हुए, राजा के उस हुक्म को ललकारते जो उनके खेत–देवालय में और भीतर तक घुसना चाहता था।

panels.shot: somber interior shot of the palace, with a grim messenger reporting to Chikka Devaraja
panels.action: Inside the palace, a dust-covered messenger kneels before Chikka Devaraja, who listens in stern silence, fingers tightened on the arm of his seat, as faint sounds of marching feet drift in from outside.

dialogue.text: The chronicles remember what followed in brief, stark lines: the king sent force, the resistance was crushed, and the Jangamas of that region paid dearly for their stand.

i18n.hi: बख़्त की किताबें आगे का हाल बस दो–चार सख़्त पंक्तियों में लिखती हैं – राजा ने फ़ौज भेजी, बग़ावत कुचल दी गई, और उस पट्टी के जंगमों ने अपने मोर्चे की भारी क़ीमत चुकाई।

panels.shot: symbolic wide shot of the road near Nanjanagudu after the crackdown, with soldiers departing and villagers grieving
panels.action: Along the road by Nanjanagudu, columns of Mysore soldiers march away in order, while behind them villagers sit on the ground in silent grief outside a damaged shrine, dust hanging thick in the still air.

dialogue.text: No bloodlines cross the palm leaves, but later voices speak of a harsh repression whose silence lay heavy over that countryside.

i18n.hi: ताड़पत्र वंशावली ख़ून की धार नहीं बताती, पर बाद की आवाज़ें सख़्त दमन की बात करती हैं, जिसकी चुप्पी उस देहात पर सालों तक भारी रही।

panels.shot: interior shot of the Attara Kacheri hall at dusk, with clerks working under lamplight
panels.action: As dusk falls, the Attara Kacheri hall glows with oil lamps, clerks still bent over records, a faint breeze stirring hanging maps while Chikka Devaraja stands at the doorway, half figure, half shadow.

dialogue.text: By the turn of the century, Mysore’s state had changed; its new bureaucracy linked fort to village, coin to decree, all threaded through the eighteen offices that bore his mark.

i18n.hi: सदी के मोड़ तक मैसूर का राज बदल चुका था – नई कचेरी-व्यवस्था ने किले को गाँव से, सिक्के को फ़रमान से बाँध दिया, सब अठारह दफ़्तरों की डोर से जो उस की मुहर रखते थे।

panels.shot: time-lapse style wide shot: the same hall imagined later under different rulers, fading back to his thoughtful face
panels.action: The Attara Kacheri hall is shown in faint overlays under later rulers and in a more modern guise, before the image fades back to a close view of an older Chikka Devaraja, eyes distant, as if weighing unseen accounts.

dialogue.text: Today we remember Chikka Devaraja as the builder of offices and order, yet his story reminds us that good governance must be measured not only by its systems, but by the lives bent under their weight.

i18n.hi: आज हम चिक्का देवराज को दफ़्तर और अनुशासन का निर्माता याद करते हैं, पर उसकी कहानी जताती है कि अच्छे राज को सिर्फ़ उसके निज़ाम से नहीं, उन ज़िंदगियों से भी तौलना होगा जो उनके बोझ तले झुकीं।

title_i18n.hi: चिक्का देवराज ने बनाई अठारह कचेरियाँ

subtitle_i18n.en: Eighteen Offices for a Restless Kingdom
subtitle_i18n.hi: बेचैन राज्य के लिए अठारह दफ़्तर
